LESSON: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.5: Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are some words are commonly misspelt?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts
2. spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency
3. value the importance of correct spelling in written communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the importance of correct spelling in written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the importance of correct spelling in written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the importance of correct spelling in written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the importance of correct spelling in written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling to a partner. (skill: spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the importance of correct spelling in written communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts.
3. Practise this skill: spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency.
4. Practise this skill: value the importance of correct spelling in written communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are some words are commonly misspelt?
2. Why is it important to spell words correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts.
5. Be able to: spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
